detailed_rationale:
Choice International is a diversified financial-services holding company (stock broking & distribution, investment banking, NBFC lending, wealth management, and a distinctive government infrastructure/policy advisory business) with a genuinely long track record: median sales growth of 21.7% over 10 years and a 5-year profit CAGR of 67%, not a recent flash. FY26 (year ended March 2026) revenue was Rs 1,119 crore (+21% YoY) and net profit Rs 238 crore (+46% YoY, profit growing faster than revenue), with a fresh, verifiable forward pipeline: the company disclosed winning government mandates worth Rs 191.38 crore across Bihar, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and other states (July 2026), and SEBI approved it as sponsor for a new AIF (Wealthwave Capital Trust), both genuine new-business developments rather than base-rate extrapolation.

Two items deserve plain treatment rather than being smoothed into the financial-sector D/E exemption: first, borrowings rose from Rs 679 crore to Rs 908 crore (+34% YoY), which is largely attributable to the NBFC lending book (an expected, business-model-consistent use of leverage for a lending entity, covered by the standard exemption). Second, and more specifically worth flagging, debtor days rose from 114 to 142 -- a genuine working-capital/collections deterioration signal that sits outside the pure-leverage exemption and should be watched on its own terms, since slower collections in a group with a lending arm can be an early asset-quality tell rather than noise. Despite the strong multi-year growth record, ROE (15.9%) and ROCE (17.3%) are only moderate, not exceptional, which tempers how much of the trailing growth rate should be credited to clean, high-return compounding versus growth funded by an expanding capital/leverage base -- a nuance the ~79x trailing PE does not appear to price in cheaply.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold on both windows; fresh research is broadly consistent, showing a real, long-track-record diversified financial franchise with fresh government-mandate wins, but also a genuine (if not extreme) working-capital deterioration signal (debtor days up from 114 to 142) and a very rich ~79x multiple against only moderate ROE/ROCE. That combination of real quality plus a demanding valuation and a specific collections flag is consistent with Hold rather than either extreme.
summary: Choice International is a diversified financial-services group spanning stock broking, NBFC lending, wealth management, and a notable government infrastructure-advisory business, with a genuinely long history of strong growth and recent new government contract wins. Profit has grown faster than revenue, which is a good sign, though the number of days it takes to collect payments has risen, which is worth watching. The stock is priced at a demanding valuation relative to its actual returns on capital. We rate it a Hold: a real, diversified growth franchise, but not cheaply priced, with a collections trend that deserves attention.
positive_para: A 10-year median sales growth of 21.7% and 5-year profit CAGR of 67% reflect a genuinely long and diversified growth track record, not a one-year flash, further supported by fresh, verifiable new business (Rs 191.38 crore in government advisory mandates won across multiple states, plus a new SEBI-approved AIF sponsorship). Profit growing faster than revenue (46% vs 21% in FY26) suggests improving operating efficiency across the group's diversified segments.
negative_para: Debtor days rose from 114 to 142, a genuine collections/working-capital deterioration that is worth monitoring in its own right, separate from the NBFC book's leverage growth (borrowings +34% YoY, which is more readily explained by the lending business model). ROE (15.9%) and ROCE (17.3%) are only moderate, not exceptional, despite the strong historical growth rate, and the stock's ~79x trailing earnings multiple and 11.1x book value already price in continuation of the fast growth -- a combination that leaves limited room for the working-capital trend to worsen further without consequence.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~79x trailing earnings against ROE of only 15.9%, the multiple is pricing continued high-20s-to-30%+ growth that only moderate returns on capital do not cleanly support -- this looks rich relative to the underlying return profile, even though the top-line growth track record is genuinely long and real. The rising debtor days add a further reason for caution on quality rather than just price.
